title: Simplify the work-readiness gate to the checks that have caught something

outcomes.statement: The work-readiness gate enforces only mechanisms that have caught a real failure or close a gap the retro identified, so its cost is proportional to what it prevents.
outcomes.demo: WR_* codes raised by enforcement and readiness-subsystem LOC are measured before and after each child and trend down; check-all returns the same verdict for all 17 existing artifacts at every step.

outcomes.statement: Already-approved history stays readable and digest-verifiable without carrying its verification machinery forward.
outcomes.demo: check-all validates all 17 artifacts with no trust map provisioned; the 20 signed and 42 unsigned ledger decision records both validate.

uncertainties.statement: Whether removing signature verification breaks validation of the 20 already-signed historical decision records (success criterion 3).
uncertainties.resolution: Measured before cutting: validateDecisionRecordShape enforces an exact-length closed key set and the ledger holds two shapes (20 signed / 42 legacy). The replacement makes the attestation keys optional-but-accepted rather than flipping a flag, so both validate. Verified against a pre-cut baseline: identical verdict for all 17 artifacts.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the WR_BOOTSTRAP_* codes are part of the signing ceremony, as the design states.
uncertainties.resolution: They are not. WR_BOOTSTRAP_EXPIRED / WR_BOOTSTRAP_PATH_UNAUTHORIZED guard CHG-022's one-time authorization window and path scope; WR_BOOTSTRAP_CHECKPOINT_DEVIATION_REQUIRED belongs to the checkpoint clock. They survive the signing cut.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the checkpoint-clock removal can land without the dual-ledger collapse.
uncertainties.resolution: It cannot, safely. The design's own §3 says the artifact-side checkpoints[] exists only to mirror the clock, so landing §2 alone leaves validateCheckpointEvidence, terminalCompletionSolelySupersedesCheckpoint and hasBootstrapCheckpointDeviation dead-but-passing — the theatre Rollout §3 forbids. C2 and C3 are declared as one child with a depends_on edge, not two.

partitions.title: Retire Ed25519 approval signing, keeping signed history readable
partitions.outcome: Approval decisions are digest-bound records with a named human approver and no cryptographic attestation; the 20 already-signed records still validate.
partitions.demo: With WORK_READINESS_APPROVAL_KEYS_JSON unset, check-all validates all 17 artifacts (pre-cut it validated zero and failed WR_APPROVAL_TRUST_UNAVAILABLE).

uncertainties.statement: Whether removing signature verification breaks the 20 signed historical records.
uncertainties.resolution: Attestation keys become optional-but-accepted, not absent. Verified against a pre-cut baseline: identical verdict for all 17 artifacts.

partitions.title: Replace the wall-clock lock with a task-boundary self-report and collapse to one ledger
partitions.outcome: No git-timestamp checkpoint can force a stop disconnected from task structure, and the artifact no longer carries a checkpoints[] array that must byte-match the feedback log.
partitions.demo: A work item whose commits span more than 90 minutes of git time passes check-staged; the artifact schema no longer accepts checkpoints[], and no WR_CHECKPOINT_* or WR_EXECUTION_ANCHOR_* code is reachable.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the clock removal and the dual-ledger collapse can be separate children.
uncertainties.resolution: They cannot be separated safely — the artifact side mirrors the clock, so landing the clock removal alone leaves three checkpoint validators dead-but-passing. Declared as one child.

partitions.title: Collapse the fine-grained git-plumbing codes to one message-carrying error
partitions.outcome: The residual git operations raise a single WR_GIT_ERROR carrying the underlying message, instead of twelve variants distinguishing shades of the same failure.
partitions.demo: Every WR_GIT_* variant except WR_GIT_ERROR is absent from enforcement, and the git-failure tests assert the carried message rather than a code taxonomy.

partitions.title: Reconcile the documented and schema-declared code set with what enforcement can raise
partitions.outcome: WORK_READINESS.md and work-readiness.schema.json declare exactly the codes the implementation can raise — no more phantom codes.
partitions.demo: A check comparing the codes named in the doc and schema against those raised in scripts/work-readiness{.mjs,/} reports an empty symmetric difference.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the doc/schema code set matches the implementation today.
uncertainties.resolution: It does not: 115 codes appear across doc+schema+implementation but only 92 were referenced in the implementation before this CHG, so 23 are declared and unraisable. Measured 2026-09-05.
